Title: Mora Simulator
Summary: Mora Simulator is a chaotic sandbox game developed in Unity (C#) for the VTuber MoraMunch, heavily inspired by the physics-driven gameplay of Goat Simulator. As the sole programmer I built a range of systems - from an implementation of Wave Function Collapse procedural generation to a custom physics system that makes explosions and buoyancy simpler. This project was made in collaboration with Devo, an artist friend of mine from the USA.

Description.Backrooms Generator (Wave Function Colla:
I implemented a real-time procedural Backrooms generator unsing a constraint-based approach based on Wave Function Collapse. Instead of generating a full map upfront, th system continuously generates and removes tiles around the player using a coroutine-driven streaming model.

Tiles are defined as prefabs with edge signatures, and valid adjacency is resolved through a constraint map. Each tile variant is expanded into all 4 rotations at runtime, allowing reuse of assets while maintaining valid edge matching. During generation, positions are selected based on lowest entropy (fewest valid tiles), and a weighted random selection is applied to introduce controlled variation.

The system maintains a custom dictionary-backed grid structure with event hooks (onAdd and onRemove) to handle GameObject instantiation and cleanup. Generation expands outward by enqueueing valid neighboring positions based on tile edge data, rather than relying on a fixed grid.

To support performance, tiles are only generated within a configurable distance from the player and removed when outside that area, effectively creating an infinite environment. Importantly, unloaded tiles are not preserved - when revisiting an area, it can regenerate into a different valid configuration. This intentionally breaks spacial consistency, creating a non-Euclidean, disorienting effect that closely matches the unpredictable nature of the Backrooms.

Description.Physics System - Physics Object: I developed a base PhysicsObject system using Unity's Rigidbody component that standardizes interactions across all dynamic entities. It supports buoyancy (called on every PhysicsObject every FixedUpdate on a custom PhysicsFluid, of course checking if any of its colliders overlaps the fluid's bounds), explosions (called from a custom Explosion before it deletes itself), and collision-based responses. Objects dispatch events such as OnKickedEvent, OnExplosionEvent, and OnCollisionEnterEvent, which are subscribed to by a method to play sound on collisions and by other scripts. For example, DestructibleObject subscribes to all three events and invokes its OnBreakEvent if the impulse exceeds a threshold that can be set in the inspector - allowing for behaviors like explosive cylinders detonating when they receive a sufficiently powerful impact.
Description.Physics System - Ragdoll: Ragdoll extends PhysicsObject, it is modified to support segmented ragdoll objects composed of multiple objects with the custom RagdollBone component. Physics are applied per bone, allowing for less rigid character movement in response to for example explosions. It includes a system to toggle between enabled (physics-driven) and disabled (animation-driven).
Description.Physics System - Flammable: I made a custom Flammable component that allows objects to ignite, burn for a certain amount of ticks (1 tick = 0.5 seconds), and spread fire other objects with the Flammable component if they are close enough. When it stops burning it invokes an OnBurnEnd event. This event can be used to for example swap a wooden crate for a burnt one or to detonate explosive cylinders.
Description.Physics System - IEdible: I made an IEdible interface (public bool CanEat(), public void Eat()). This lets the player eat for example the "nuclear taco" to cause a huge explosion or a dead NPC to turn them into an egg. (NPC → egg was not my idea, but I was asked to make that so I did)
